opening.headline: When product quality gradually declines after launch, learn how and at what frequency to reevaluate in order to detect the decline early.
body: When launched, the system passed evaluation, but user complaints may gradually increase over several weeks. This represents a gradual decline rather than a sharp drop, so it does not become apparent through a single incident report. Google's operations excellence documentation notes that AI systems may change over time due to data, environment, and model variations, and recommends that operations teams maintain observability during ongoing use.

In this course, we first examine how to categorize monitoring metrics into quality, cost, and safety domains to build dashboards. Next, we learn how to define monitoring cycles—ongoing, periodic, and change-based—along with thresholds and alerts, and follow through two case studies demonstrating early detection of downward trends.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can describe the metrics and intervals of operational quality monitoring.
Monitoring metrics can be categorized into quality, cost, and safety domains.

screens.title: Quality gradually deteriorates after launch.
screens.lead: First, read about the situation where quality gradually declines after initial release.

visual.alt: Two-line graph showing a gradual decline in quality metrics and a slight increase in complaint numbers after launch.
labels: One incident report covers invisible segments

paragraphs: Let's assume that a document summarization service has been launched. At the time of launch, it passed evaluations and received positive user feedback. However, after a few weeks, requests and complaints for revising the summaries gradually increase.

This decline is not a sharp drop but a gradual one. The service did not stop and errors are rare, so it cannot be captured by a single incident report. It is only when the responsible person notices that the quality has already significantly deteriorated.

The causes can be multiple. Changes can occur due to altered distributions of incoming input data, model updates, or changes in surrounding tools. Google documents explain that systems detect data drift and performance degradation during operation, while generative AI monitors changes in output quality and safety compliance. The question posed in this course is: what should be monitored, and at what frequency, to detect declines early?

callout.label: Things to think about
callout.text: The fact that the service is running normally is not the same as the fact that the quality of the response content is normal.

screens.outro: First, let's recall which indicator we are currently viewing.

screens.title: What metrics do you use to report operational quality?
screens.lead: When you select each question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. You won't have to enter or submit your answer, so think about it in your head first and then press it.

items.prompt: Are there any metrics to monitor service status, such as response time or error rate?
items.answer: Service health metrics are the first metrics to establish. Google documents recommend viewing latency, error rate, and resource utilization through Cloud Monitoring. However, these metrics only indicate whether a service is running, not whether the response content is correct.

items.prompt: Is there an indicator to verify whether the response content is correct?
items.answer: The quality of the content must be assessed separately. A typical approach involves repeatedly evaluating bundles of criteria such as instruction adherence, factual accuracy, and consistency with evidence. Without such metrics, it would be impossible to recognize situations where a service operates normally but the quality degrades.

items.prompt: Is there a metric to see how costs are increasing?
items.answer: Cost is also part of operational quality. By examining call volume, token usage, and service-specific costs over time, you can understand changes after modifying prompts or models. Cost metrics are easy to correlate with quality metrics when viewed on the same time axis.

screens.outro: Now we will examine how to configure a dashboard across the quality, cost, and safety domains.

screens.title: Quality, cost, safety indicator dashboard configuration
screens.lead: Select each tab to view metrics by area within the dashboard.

visual.alt: A monitoring dashboard divided into four sections: quality, availability, cost, and security.

tabs.label: quality
tabs.body:
This area assesses the quality of the response content. It evaluates aspects such as instruction adherence, factual accuracy, consistency with evidence, response length, and tone, continuously measuring these criteria. Google documents explain that it tracks changes in the output quality of generative AI and sets up alerts when changes are detected.

Without this area, it would be impossible to know that a service is functioning normally yet delivering poor content.

tabs.label: Availability
tabs.body:
This area monitors service **state**. It examines request volume, error rates, and latency at the endpoint level. Google documents recommend viewing latency, error rates, and resource utilization metrics through Cloud Monitoring to identify bottlenecks.

These metrics quickly alert you to outages, but they do not detect a decline in content quality.

tabs.label: cost
tabs.body:
View call volume, token usage, and service costs. Google's cost optimization documentation explains labeling resources to differentiate costs by project, team, and activity, and tracking through dashboards and budget alerts.

OpenAI's operations documentation distinguishes between expenditure alerts and hard expenditure limits. Alerts notify when usage exceeds thresholds, while hard limits stop API traffic when the limit is reached.

tabs.label: safety
tabs.body:
The ratio of responses classified as safety violations, along with cases reviewed by humans, is shown. Google Docs advises tracking safety indicators to detect harmful content generated by generative AI models and setting up alerts accordingly.

Safety metrics typically remain at low levels under normal conditions, but they serve as the first signal to respond to when changes occur.

screens.outro: The indicator has been set; now I'll show you how to determine how frequently inventory updates are sent and when they are notified.

screens.title: Monitoring interval and thresholds, alerts
screens.lead: Move the slider to step through and verify the individual roles of monitoring frequency, threshold values, and alerts.

stops.body: Metrics such as error rate, latency, and request volume that can be viewed in real time. These indicators quickly notify you of issues such as service outages or slowdowns. When values exceed predefined thresholds, they are immediately triggered to send alerts.

This is an indicator for periodically running response quality evaluations. Items such as instruction adherence and evidence alignment fall under this evaluation bundle. The OpenAI evaluation documentation recommends expanding evaluation bundles to identify new non-deterministic cases during operations.

This is an indicator that re-runs the same evaluation every time the model or prompt changes. The OpenAI documentation explains that continuous evaluation should be set up to evaluate after each change, allowing immediate verification of the impact right after the change.

This is the threshold for triggering alerts. Google's cost documentation recommends setting alert thresholds for each KPI, but advises setting them at meaningful levels to avoid alert fatigue. For example, an alert configuration is triggered when accuracy drops below a certain level.

If the threshold is exceeded, it is communicated to the responsible party, and corrective actions such as prompt reconfiguration or rollback may follow as needed. Alerts become noise if it is not predefined who will take what action.

screens.outro: After the alarm has sounded, let's examine how a person intervenes.

screens.title: Human review and feedback loop
screens.lead: Select the right arrow to verify each link sequentially, classify the cause, and take action after the alert sounds.

steps.title: Aligns automated evaluation with human judgment
steps.body: Automated evaluation has the advantage of scalability, but it must be periodically corrected to align with human judgment. Google Docs introduces a workflow where nuanced aspects are evaluated through human-in-the-loop assessment.

steps.title: Classifies the cause when an alert sounds
steps.body: It determines whether the input distribution has changed, whether the model has changed, or whether the prompt has changed. Actions must vary based on the root cause, so classification is required first. If you change the model without first classifying the cause, the issue will remain unresolved when the root cause is actually a change in input distribution.

steps.title: Take appropriate actions based on the cause.
steps.body: If the input distribution has changed, strengthen the evaluation bundle; if it's a prompt issue, adjust the prompt; if the model change is the cause, retrain the model.

steps.title: Reflects the action results in metrics and thresholds.
steps.body: Verify the results against the metrics again, and adjust thresholds if they are too sensitive or too lenient. This loop must continue so that monitoring remains effective over time. Instead of keeping fixed thresholds, continuously review and adjust them based on the accuracy of alerts—both true positives and false positives.

screens.outro: Now let's follow the process of detecting quality degradation early through an example.

screens.title: Explanation: Indicator for early detection of quality decline
screens.lead: The instructor explains the process of identifying the causes of quality decline in the document summarization service. Select the right arrow to proceed to the next step.

steps.title: case
steps.body: The number of user modification requests in the document summarization service is gradually increasing. The responsible party wants to know whether the service has failed or its quality has degraded.

steps.title: Excludes service status issues
steps.body: Verify if the error rate and latency are normal. If they are normal, it means the service is not experiencing a state-related issue, allowing the root cause to be narrowed down to the response content.

steps.title: Observe the trend of regular quality assessments
steps.body: Review the trend of basis alignment and compliance adherence in regular quality assessments. A gradual decline in the values indicates actual deterioration in quality. The key is to examine trends, not values at a single point in time.

steps.title: Evaluates the input distribution against a benchmark bundle.
steps.body: Compares the distribution of recent inputs against the composition of the evaluation bundle. If a new type of document not previously present has appeared in the evaluation bundle, the evaluation passes but the actual input has changed.

steps.title: Strengthens the bundle and updates the threshold.
steps.body: Add the new type to the evaluation bundle and adjust the prompt. Then, re-run the same evaluation to verify recovery and update the threshold.

steps.title: result
steps.body: Service status indicators alone were not sufficient to detect this decline. We must examine both the evaluation trend and the input distribution together to detect it early. We also do not forget to retain new types in evaluation bundles to prevent the same issue from recurring.

screens.outro: This time, we will look at an example of reading both cost and safety signals together.

screens.title: Explanation: Reading cost and safety signals together
screens.lead: The following is a hypothetical weekly inspection record. By selecting the displayed sections, you can view how the signals from three areas are interpreted simultaneously at the same time.

data.text:
Weekly Review Log (hypothetical example)  
Week 3: Average response length 300 tokens, monthly cost increase rate +2%, unsafe response rate 0.1%  
Week 4: Prompt modification deployment (additional explanation sentence)  
Week 5: Average response length of 520 tokens, monthly cost increase rate of +21%, Safety violation response rate: 0.3%  
Action: Adjust the output length specification and measure again in week 6.

marks.span: Average response length of 520 tokens, monthly cost increase rate of +21%
marks.note: As response lengths increased, so did costs. By dividing token usage by service label, you can identify which service experienced the increase. OpenAI documentation explains that latency is significantly affected by both model and generated token count, meaning increased length could impact both latency and cost.
Prompt modifications occurred in weeks when costs and durations changed. Aligning the indicator change point with the change history is the fastest way to narrow down the root cause.

The response rate to safety violations also changed at the same time point. If viewed separately by the three areas, this relationship might be overlooked; therefore, they should be viewed on the same screen with the same time axis.

marks.span: Adjust the output length specification and measure again in week 6.
marks.note: Actions to adjust length limitations and output format specifications, and to verify again whether the indicators have recovered. Only by linking these adjustments with the subsequent measurement can we determine whether the actions were effective.

screens.outro: Now I will summarize the components discussed so far.

screens.title: Composition of Operational Quality Monitoring
screens.lead: We list the elements involved in operational quality monitoring in sequence.

paragraphs: **Metrics** are divided into three areas: quality, cost, and safety. The quality area includes both evaluation of response content and service status, and these two aspects cannot substitute for each other.

**Cycles** are divided into continuous, periodic, and change-based. Service status is monitored continuously, response quality is checked periodically, and model or prompt changes are verified on a change-based basis immediately after the update.

**Thresholds and Alerts** are set at meaningful levels to reduce alert fatigue. Alerts must be paired with responsible personnel and clear action paths. The results of the actions are then reflected back into the metrics and thresholds. The absence of metrics makes it impossible to detect a decline—this was the foundational premise of this course.

callout.label: Core
callout.text: You must read the three areas on the same time axis to identify the root cause.

checks.explain: If error rates and latency are normal, service state issues can be ruled out, and subtle quality degradation can only be identified by examining trends in evaluation metrics together with changes in input distribution.

wrong.0: A smooth decline does not manifest as a single incident report like a sharp drop, so it can only be observed and detected late.
wrong.2: The issue is not error rate but content quality; lowering the threshold only increases alert fatigue.

glossary.def: A value that displays the quality of a service in operation, either numerically or by judgment. Examples include compliance, evidence consistency, and error rate.
This is the interval for verifying indicators divided into ongoing, periodic, and change-based checks.
This is the threshold value beyond which an alert is triggered.
There are too many meaningless notifications, causing important notifications to be ignored.
This is a phenomenon where the nature of data arriving during operation differs from that observed during evaluation.

misconceptions.myth: If it passes pre-release evaluation, quality is maintained.
misconceptions.fact: Data and environment changes, or model variations, can lead to a decline in quality. Evaluation must continue throughout operations.

misconceptions.myth: If the error rate and delay are normal, then the quality is also normal.
misconceptions.fact: Service state and response content quality are separate entities. Content quality must be measured using independent metrics.
Automated evaluation must be periodically aligned and corrected against human judgment.

closing.lead: This summarizes the core content of the class.
points: Without indicators, you cannot know about a decline.
Quality, cost, and safety are read on the same time axis.
Thresholds and alerts are defined together with the action path.
